statement: Let n = len(nums). For each nonempty subset S of {0,...,n-1}, define P(S) = product over i in S of nums[i]. The function returns a result r and r is the maximum value of P(S) over all nonempty subsets S; that is, (a) there exists a nonempty S with r = P(S), and (b) for every nonempty S, P(S) <= r.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 13, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -9 <= nums[i] <= 9.

statement: The function returns a result r; it does not fail due to i64 overflow, out-of-bounds indexing, or panic.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 13, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -9 <= nums[i] <= 9.

statement: Let n = len(nums). Whenever the function returns a result r, there exists a nonempty subset S of {0,...,n-1} with r = product over i in S of nums[i]. Moreover: if r > 0, S can be chosen with nums[i] != 0 for all i in S and with an even number of indices i in S satisfying nums[i] < 0; if r < 0, S can be chosen with nums[i] != 0 for all i in S and with an odd number of such indices; if r = 0, S can be chosen containing an index i with nums[i] = 0.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 13, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -9 <= nums[i] <= 9.

statement: Let n = len(nums). Whenever the function returns a result r, for every nonempty subset S of {0,...,n-1}, product over i in S of nums[i] <= r.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 13, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -9 <= nums[i] <= 9.

statement: Let n = len(nums). Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < n, r >= nums[i].
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 13, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -9 <= nums[i] <= 9.

statement: Let n = len(nums). Whenever the function returns a result r, r < 0 if and only if n = 1 and nums[0] < 0.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 13, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -9 <= nums[i] <= 9.

statement: The function returns a result r and r = nums[0].
Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 0.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 13, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), nums[i] = 0.

statement: Let n = len(nums). Whenever the function returns a result r, r = product over i = 0 to n-1 of nums[i].
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 13, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -9 <= nums[i] <= 9 and nums[i] > 0.

statement: Let n = len(nums) and let Prod = product over i = 0 to n-1 of nums[i]. Whenever the function returns a result r: if n = 1, then r = nums[0]; if n >= 2 and n is even, then r = Prod; if n >= 2 and n is odd, then r = Prod / m, where m is the largest value among nums[0],...,nums[n-1] (the negative entry closest to zero), and the division is exact.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 13, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -9 <= nums[i] <= 9 and nums[i] < 0.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = nums[j].
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 13, for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -9 <= nums[i] <= 9, and there exists j with 0 <= j < len(nums) such that nums[j] > 0 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and i != j, nums[i] = 0.

statement: Let n = len(nums) and let negCount be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < n and nums[i] < 0. Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 0 if and only if (there exists i with 0 <= i < n and nums[i] = 0) and (for every i with 0 <= i < n, nums[i] <= 0) and negCount <= 1.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 13, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -9 <= nums[i] <= 9.

statement: Let N = {i | 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] != 0}. Whenever the function returns a result r, r = product over i in N of nums[i].
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 13, for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -9 <= nums[i] <= 9, there exists i with nums[i] != 0, and the number of indices i with nums[i] < 0 is even.

statement: Let N = {i | 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] != 0}. Let m be the largest value among the negative entries, i.e. m = max { nums[i] | 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] < 0 }. Whenever the function returns a result r, r = (product over i in N of nums[i]) / m, and the division is exact.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 13, for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -9 <= nums[i] <= 9, the number of indices i with nums[i] < 0 is odd, and either there exists i with nums[i] > 0 or the number of negative entries is at least 3.

statement: Let n = len(nums). For every slice nums' of length n that is a permutation of nums (there is a bijection pi on {0,...,n-1} with nums'[j] = nums[pi(j)] for every j), the function returns the same result on nums' as on nums; both calls return results and their results are equal.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 13, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -9 <= nums[i] <= 9.

statement: Let n = len(nums). Whenever the function returns a result r, if r > 0 then for every i with 0 <= i < n and nums[i] > 1 there exists an integer k such that r = nums[i] * k.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 13, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -9 <= nums[i] <= 9.
